Continue this exact scene as one unbroken locked-off shot. The camera is on a tripod and does not move at all — no push, no pan, no tilt, no shake, no cut.

Two commuters cross the frame in opposite directions, each absorbed in their own errand.

The man in the rust-orange corduroy jacket walks steadily from LEFT to RIGHT along the foreground, reading the phone in his right hand. He keeps reading it for the whole shot, his head tilted DOWN AND TO THE RIGHT, and he walks out of frame at the RIGHT edge at a normal commuter pace.

The woman in the deep-teal wool overcoat walks steadily from RIGHT to LEFT through the mid-ground, holding her paper coffee cup. She keeps reading the hanging departure board for the whole shot, her chin raised and her head turned UP AND TO THE LEFT, and she continues toward the LEFT of frame.

Their two paths simply cross. Each keeps their own head position the entire time: his stays down on the phone, hers stays up on the board. No one turns their head, no one changes direction, no one stops, no one speaks, no one waves, no one greets anyone. Both simply continue on their own routes at their own steady pace.

Around them the evening rush crowd keeps flowing in both directions with natural motion blur, everyone in muted charcoal, black, navy, beige and grey. Nobody looks at the camera. Lighting, wardrobe and framing stay exactly as they are.

Observational documentary cinematography on a long lens, compressed perspective, shallow depth of field, restrained naturalistic grade, fine film grain. No dialogue, no speech, no music. No text, no subtitles, no captions.
